intended_object: The canonical additive isomorphism R^{(ι)} ⊗_R N ≅ N^{(ι)}, where R^{(ι)} is the free right R-module on ι, R is a possibly noncommutative ring and N is a left R-module. It sends (r_i)_i ⊗ n to (r_i n)_i. Inferred from the docstring and the names of the component maps.
explanation:
The forward map is `freeToFinsupp`. It is the lift of a balanced map that sends x ⊗ n to Σ_i single i (unop(x_i) • n), which is the coordinatewise evaluation (r_i) ⊗ n ↦ (r_i n). The inverse sends single i n to single i 1 ⊗ n. The two round trips are proved, so the result really is the standard isomorphism.

The setting is already the natural one: any ring R, which need not be commutative, any index type ι and any left R-module N. A right R-module is encoded as a `Module Rᵐᵒᵖ` instance, and the free right module as `ι →₀ Rᵐᵒᵖ`, which is correct. The isomorphism is additive (`≃+`) because a balanced tensor product over a noncommutative ring is in general only an abelian group.

Mathlib's counterpart `TensorProduct.finsuppScalarLeft` gives the same isomorphism, but only over commutative semirings. Mathlib has no balanced tensor product over noncommutative rings, so this definition is not a narrower copy of an existing Mathlib construction.
